title: Finance Note: Working Out a Coverage Year's Benefit Allowance
content:
**Scope.** This note works out the benefit granted afresh for a coverage year on a plan of the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans.

**1. The allowance the grant rests on.** The benefit granted afresh for a coverage year is the yearly benefit allowance the coverage sets for the piece.

**2. What the plan drew in the coverage year just ended.** What the plan drew in the coverage year just ended is the benefit consumed by the settlements booked to it in the 12 months to the handling date.

**3. How much is granted.** The whole of that yearly benefit allowance is granted.

**4. Time since the anniversary.** The grant is not reduced for the time that has passed since the anniversary.

**5. Inspections.** The grant is not reduced for the inspections logged in the year.

**6. Membership.** The grant carries no membership uplift.

**7. The lifetime ceiling.** What is granted is limited to what is left of the coverage's lifetime benefit ceiling after the allowance entries already booked to the plan, and nothing unused in the coverage year just ended carries forward. What is left of that ceiling is never less than nothing.

**8. Order and rounding.** The shares and the uplift all act on the yearly benefit allowance, one after another and each on the figure the one before it left, and the lifetime ceiling is applied only to the figure they leave. The amount granted is rounded to two decimal places once at the end.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

Coverage whose yearly benefit allowance is 2500.00 USD and whose lifetime benefit ceiling is 7500.00 USD carries allowance entries already booked to the plan coming to 6000.00 USD. The allowance the grant rests on is 2500.00 USD and the whole of it is granted, so the figure reaching the ceiling is 2500.00 USD. What is left of the lifetime ceiling is 7500.00 USD less 6000.00 USD, being 1500.00 USD, and the grant is limited to that. The amount granted is 1500.00 USD once the figure is rounded to two decimal places at the end.
